title: Require identifying labels for strategic-typed children at creation
description:
During the 2821e177 (addressing-v2) fan-out, the breakdown-review gate failed its first round solely because all six `type:story` children lacked their own `story:<slug>` label. The content standard (`.claude/skills/jit-manage/references/content-standards.md`, Strategic Labels) requires every strategic-typed issue to carry its own identifying kebab-slug label, and the jit-breakdown content lint (Step 7) checks it, but nothing in the creation path (Step 6a) or the analysis JSON contract demands it, so the defect is caught only post-hoc by an expensive AI gate round.

Move the check to creation time in `.claude/skills/jit-breakdown/SKILL.md`: when a created child's type is strategic or carries its own membership namespace in `[type_hierarchy.label_associations]` (for example a story child whose tasks will later carry `story:<slug>`), the creation step derives and attaches the child's identifying label at `jit issue create` time, and the Step 5 pre-approval quality bar lists it alongside clean titles and non-empty gate tiers.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: the jit-breakdown creation step (6a) attaches an identifying `<namespace>:<slug>` label to every created child whose type has a membership namespace in the configured label associations, derived from the child title as a kebab slug.
- [hard] REQ-02: the Step 5 pre-approval quality bar names the identifying-label requirement so a missing slug is caught before any issue is created.
- [hard] REQ-03: a fan-out containing strategic-typed children passes the breakdown-review content-standards check without a label-related finding on the first round after the change.
